lsm.busy.calls_one: {n} call with side effects hasn't finished: {calls}
lsm.busy.calls_other: {n} calls with side effects haven't finished: {calls}
lsm.notLinked: Ergo isn't connected to the service manager (it wasn't started by the service manager)
lsm.disconnected: Lost the connection to the service manager; the full status pushed after reconnecting is what counts
lsm.closed: The connection to the service manager has been closed
lsm.notConnected: Not connected to the service manager yet (or the connection dropped)
lsm.unsupported: This version of the service manager doesn't support owned services
lsm.busy.restartHold: The secretary just queued an idle restart of ergo; waiting for it to finish this turn
lsm.manageUnsupported: This version of the service manager doesn't support management commands
lsm.tools.title.entries: Open or close outside access to a service
lsm.tools.state.FAILED: failed (didn't start, or exited after starting)
lsm.tools.state.ORPHAN: its port is held by a process the service manager doesn't recognize (orphan)
lsm.tools.detail.noStop: No graceful stop: it can only be force-stopped (its process killed)
lsm.tools.detail.protected: ergo depends on it: {why}. ergo can't stop, restart or remove it
lsm.tools.why.tunnel: this is ergo's tunnel to the internet; without it your phone can't reach ergo
lsm.tools.why.other: ergo needs it to run (the service manager says: {why})
lsm.tools.verb.orphanKill: kill the process on its port
lsm.tools.refuseUseRestartSelf: To restart ergo itself, use {tool} (restarts when idle, needs the user's approval).
lsm.tools.refuseByHand: ergo can't stop, restart or remove services it depends on. If it really has to be done, the user can do it on the service manager's web page.
lsm.tools.err.notLinked: ergo wasn't started by the service manager, so it can't control the services in it.
lsm.tools.err.notConnected: Not connected to the service manager right now (it may be reconnecting). Try again in a moment.
lsm.tools.err.unsupported: This version of the service manager doesn't let ergo manage other services yet. Update the service manager first.
lsm.tools.err.disconnected: The connection to the service manager dropped partway: it may or may not have happened. Check with {tool}.
lsm.tools.err.timeout: The service manager hasn't answered for a long time. That doesn't mean it didn't happen (starting waits until ready, scenarios start layer by layer). Check with {tool} in a bit.
lsm.tools.err.protected: The service manager refused (services ergo depends on can't be touched this way): {message}
lsm.tools.err.notFound: The service manager says it doesn't exist: {message}
lsm.tools.err.inUse: Something else still uses it; remove that first: {message}
lsm.tools.err.notOwner: Only project services registered by ergo can be removed; hand-written ones the user deletes on the service manager's web page: {message}
lsm.tools.err.notAllowed: The service manager doesn't let ergo do this: {message}
lsm.tools.tellTruth: Tell the user exactly this; don't say it was done.
lsm.tools.find.needService: Give a service (its name, as listed by lsm_status).
lsm.tools.find.needProfile: Give a profile (a scenario name, as listed by lsm_status).
lsm.tools.find.none: No service in the service manager matches “{query}”. There are: {list}
lsm.tools.find.ambiguous: More than one service matches “{query}”: {list}. Ask the user which one; don't pick yourself.
lsm.tools.find.noProfile: There's no scenario called “{profile}”. There are: {list}
lsm.tools.find.noProfiles: The service manager has no scenarios, so none called “{profile}”.
lsm.tools.done.pending: {name} is busy; it will stop once it's idle. That's queued.
lsm.tools.done.already: {name} was already like that; nothing to change.
lsm.tools.done.stopWhenIdle: {name} wasn't busy, so it's stopped now.
lsm.tools.done.cancelStop: Cancelled the stop-when-idle for {name}; it keeps running.
lsm.tools.done.autostartOn: Added {name} to autostart: it will start by itself after the computer restarts (it won't start right now if it isn't running).
lsm.tools.done.autostartOff: Removed {name} from autostart: it keeps running for now, but won't start by itself after the computer restarts.
lsm.tools.done.remove: Removed {name}: stopped it and took it out of the service manager.
lsm.tools.done.orphanAdopt: Adopted: the process on {name}'s port now counts as it.
lsm.tools.done.exposeOn: Opened public access to {name} (tunnel {tunnel} is up).
lsm.tools.done.exposeOnUrl: Opened public access to {name} (tunnel {tunnel} is up): {url}
lsm.tools.done.restartSelf: Queued: once ergo is idle (its tasks and running calls are done, and this reply is finished), it restarts and the service manager brings it back up; this conversation carries on afterwards. No need to wait; just let the user know.
lsm.tools.done.restartSelfAlready: Already queued: ergo restarts once it's idle, and this conversation carries on afterwards. No need to queue it again.
lsm.tools.status.empty: The service manager has no services yet.
lsm.tools.status.protectedNote: Ones marked “ergo depends on it” can't be stopped, restarted or removed through ergo.
lsm.tools.logs.cut_one: (Too long; kept only the last {n} line)
lsm.tools.logs.cut_other: (Too long; kept only the last {n} lines)
lsm.tools.logs.others: Other logs (pass source to read one): {list}
lsm.tools.done.forcedStop: {name} has no normal way to stop, so it was force-stopped (whatever it was doing was cut off).
lsm.tools.done.forcedRestart: {name} has no normal way to restart, so it was force-restarted (force-stopped, then started).
lsm.tools.err.noIdleStop: {name} doesn't report when it's busy, so there's no waiting until it's idle. If the user just wants it stopped, use stop: with no normal way to stop, it gets force-stopped right away.
